alpha_anch.name: Product of the anchorage coefficients α1 to α5 (Table 8.2)

background.text: α2 α3 α5 ≥ 0.7. Each coefficient follows from Table 8.2 (bar shape, cover, confinement by transverse reinforcement and by transverse pressure); 1.0 is always on the safe side.

refs.text: EN 1992-1-1:2004 + AC:2010 + A1:2014. Eurocode 2: Design of concrete structures. Part 1-1: General rules and rules for buildings.

alpha_cc.name: Coefficient for long-term effects on the compressive strength

background.text: The recommended value is 1.0; it should lie between 0.8 and 1.0. Several National Annexes use 0.85 for flexure and axial load (the UK Annex uses 0.85 for compression in flexure and axial loading and 1.0 otherwise). A calculation that leaves α_cc out has assumed 1.0.

alpha_ct.name: Coefficient for long-term effects on the tensile strength

alpha_imp.name: Imperfection factor of the buckling curve

background.text: The curve depends on the section type, the buckling axis, the steel grade and the plate thickness (Table 6.2): a rolled I section with h/b > 1.2 and t_f ≤ 40 mm is curve a about y–y but curve b about z–z. Curve b is the value this object opens with, not a default for every section.
